claims.explanation: WZ-4002 is a dual EGFR/ERBB2 inhibitor, and its selective killing pattern is best explained by dependence on EGFR/ERBB2 signaling. Sensitive lines include those with EGFR mutations (HCC4006, NCIH1650, KYSE270) and other RTK/RAS pathway alterations that may create addiction to ERBB signaling, while resistant lines often have mutations in parallel pathways (e.g., BRAF, NRAS, NF1, MET) that bypass EGFR/ERBB2 inhibition. High EGFR or ERBB2 expression is expected to sensitize, whereas mutations in downstream or bypass pathways confer protection.

features.basis: Activating EGFR mutations sensitize to EGFR inhibitors; observed in sensitive lines (HCC4006, NCIH1650, KYSE270).
ERBB2 kinase domain mutations can be sensitive to ERBB2 inhibitors; WZ-4002 targets ERBB2.
High EGFR expression increases dependence on EGFR signaling, enhancing sensitivity to EGFR inhibitors.
High ERBB2 expression predicts response to ERBB2-targeted therapies.
BRAF mutations activate MAPK pathway bypassing EGFR/ERBB2, observed in resistant lines (LOXIMVI, K029AX, IGR37).
NRAS mutations activate downstream signaling independent of EGFR, observed in resistant lines (IPC298, KU1919).
NF1 loss activates RAS pathway, conferring resistance to EGFR inhibitors; observed in resistant lines.
MET alterations can bypass EGFR inhibition; observed in resistant line HGC27.
KRAS mutations drive downstream signaling and are associated with resistance to EGFR inhibitors; observed in resistant lines (OV7, SNU410, GSU).
PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT pathway, potentially bypassing EGFR dependence; observed in resistant lines.
PIK3CA mutations activate PI3K pathway downstream of EGFR, reducing sensitivity; observed in resistant lines (HGC27, KYSE510).
WZ-4002 was identified as a modulator of CHST2 in glioblastoma; high CHST2 may predict response.
